question: What is the API reading in Shah Alam right now?
name: Claude
answer:
I can't pull a live reading, but the latest figures I found put Shah Alam in the **Unhealthy** range, at about 168–170.

- **Latest official-style reading:** Shah Alam was at 170 on the semakapi.my tracker, which republishes Department of Environment data hourly. That site lists it as Unhealthy.
- **Morning report on 17 Oct:** Petaling Jaya and Shah Alam each recorded 169. Another report from the same day gives Shah Alam at 168.
- **Earlier trend:** Shah Alam was at 180 as of 5pm in a Focus Malaysia report, so it has eased slightly. Other reports put it in the high 160s to 170.

**What the numbers mean:** 0–50 is good, 51–100 moderate, 101–200 unhealthy, 201–300 very unhealthy, and above 300 hazardous. At about 170, Shah Alam is in the upper half of the unhealthy band. It is not yet "very unhealthy". Sensitive groups such as children, older people and people with asthma or heart conditions should limit time outdoors. Wearing an N95 mask outside is sensible.

These figures are a few hours old and APIMS updates hourly. For the exact current number, check the Department of Environment's APIMS portal (apims.doe.gov.my) or the MyIPU app.

SHAH ALAM, Sept 19 - Shah Alam recorded one of the highest Air Pollutant Index (API) readings in the country as of 11am today, while two other areas in Selangor also recorded unhealthy air quality.

According to the Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal, Shah Alam recorded an API reading of 156, while Johan Setia and Petaling Jaya recorded readings of 118 and 109, respectively.

Several other town in Kuala Lumpur, Putrajaya, Negeri Sembilan, Johor, Melaka and Sabah also recorded unhealthy API readings.

A total of 37 areas across the country had moderate air quality, while 10 had good API readings.
